source_checks.finding: Page confirms the exact words: 'If your Microsoft cloud storage is full, you cannot send or receive email.' It also confirms the 25 MB attachment rule ('If a message has an attachment larger than 25 MB, Outlook cannot send the message'), the signature rule and the safe senders rule. The storage sentence sits in the page introduction, and the excerpt wording matches it. The user's Outlook.com account matches the stated applicability.

Page confirms the exact words 'If you can't sign in to your account, use the Microsoft account sign-in helper.' Card section label says 'step 2 (account check)' under 'Can't send mail in Outlook.com', but the page places this sentence and the password, blocked-account and sign-in helper text in the introduction above that section, not under a numbered step. Card fix: relabel the section as the introduction. Page also confirms: 'check your account: update your password if it's been changed recently' and 'Your account might also be temporarily blocked because we noticed some unusual sign-in activity.' Claims are supported.

Page confirms iPhone or iPad Mail fetch wording: Automatically is set by default with iOS 11 and later and iPadOS, and background fetch happens only while charging and on Wi-Fi. This is a correct distractor: the user uses Outlook.com in a web browser, not the iPhone Mail app, so the passage does not apply to this user and is correctly unused.

required_actions.action: Check mailbox storage, since full Microsoft cloud storage stops sending and receiving
If storage is not full, check the account and update the password if it was changed recently
If the account may be temporarily blocked for unusual sign-in activity, unblock it
If sign-in fails, use the Microsoft account sign-in helper
Keep attachments at or under 25 MB
If a signature causes an error, remove it and resend
